newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- OCT 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- OCT 18.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:
KATHIMERINI

--The direction the government will take in the economy will be decided today at a meeting chaired by National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou. Reports say the government will attempt to have the drachma enter the European Exchange Mechanism by the end of 1997 to ensure the fastest possible participation in the single currency and shape conditions for the faithful application of the convergence programme.

--New bill before Parliament foresees the gradual transformation of older 102 billion drachma bond loan by the state-run National Bank of Greece into shares, paving the way to wider participation by the private sector in the bank's share capital.

--Today's meeting of the government's economic team will make the first overall evaluation of the 1997 budget being drafted. The budget is believed to provide for 400 billion drachmas in revenues in spending cutbacks and abolition of tax exemptions and a 13 percent increases in taxes.
--Capital market will conduct weekly checks at the stock exchange as of November.
--New customs code aims to put the lid on smuggling activity.
IMERISIA

--Final decisions on the 1997 budget will be taken at today's meeting. Ten measures will characterise the budget, including the abolition of tax exemptions, non-indexation of tax brackets and freeze on subsidies.

--Government intervenes, following yesterday's clashes at TVX Gold processing plant. A delegation of four government deputy ministers in Thessaloniki today to find a peaceful solution to locals' protests.
--Intracom, Siemens to supply telecommunications organisation, OTE, with 335,000 digital switches. OTE will appoint a management team for the remaining two million switches.
KERDOS
--Head of the Capital Market Commission admits the inability to conduct effective and exhaustive supervision of financial firms and exchnages ahead of application of new law on investment services.
--All political parties favuor shedding more light on the Floisvos casino issue, but government and opposition differ on form of fact-finding commission.
EXPRESS
--Procrastination in public administration undermines government's efforts for the economy. Only 14 of 22 state-run utilities and organisations (DEKO) have prepared amendments to their charters.
--Final decisions on the budget at Cabinet meeting next week. Today's is expected to approve the spending cutbacks and tax exemption measures.
-- Despite clashes between residents and police over the TVX Gold plant, the government is determined to proceed with the investment.
NAFTEMBORIKI
--Hellenic Industrial Development Bank (ETBA) examines settling bad debts totalling 80 billion drachmas from 240 firms.
--Drastic changes planned in shipping policy and Greek merchant marine, minister says.
--Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
